The cells sit inside the dossier's own 'New Mexico (province)' region (2,208 cells), which already contains the whole state. safavid-dynasty_1609 is the dossier's correction (Cliopatria 1609 minus Kandahar and Iraq) plus the exact regions of Safavid ledger/38-40. The page supports every date: Tabriz 'on 21 October 1603', Nakhchivan entered 'at the same month', Yerevan captured 'in June' 1604, and 'Ganja, Baku, Shirvan, and Shamakhi in Azerbaijan in June 1606'. Cliopatria's 1609 Safavid shape holds only 16 cells in Azerbaijan and Armenia (gazetteer), so the dossier's snap did erase the gains. In the trial the snap removes 2 cells instead of 370. The Ottoman/Safavid overlap is 0, and the Cliopatria Safavid 1612 shape holds 420 Azerbaijan and Armenia cells, so the next keyframe keeps the land. A minor reach is inherited from ledger/39: the Yerevan 100 km disc covers 30 Turkish cells (Igdir 15, Agri 8, Kars 7), which the Safavids already held from 1604.

Replacing the dossier's 250 km Tabriz disc and its whole-country cuts with the Safavid gain regions did keep Van (43 cells), Hakkari (26), the Iraqi Kurdistan edge (34) and West Azarbaijan (32) Ottoman, as they were in 1608. That part is right: the page has the Ottoman commander 'withdraw to the fortress of Van'. But dropping {country: Azerbaijan} and {country: Armenia} made the 1609 snap hand the Ottomans 47 unowned Karabakh cells (Kelbajar 9, Aghdam 6, Khojavend 6, Lankaran 6, Zangilan 4 and more). Those cells had been nobody's since kingdom-of-artsakh dissolved in 1603. The Principality of Khachen page says 'In 1603 the Persians established a protectorate over the Khamsa', and the Ottoman ledger already loses Armenia (June 1604) and Azerbaijan (June 1606). That was an unexplained Ottoman reconquest, not 'stays Ottoman'. I added both countries back to the subtraction and updated the text and why. The trial now gives ottoman-empire_1609 added 686 / removed 882 (published 686/1034, before the fix 733/882). The 47 cells stay unowned, as they were from 1603 to 1608.
